$comment: The MCP/SDK receipt surface and the CLI/API transaction surface name the same
settled payment differently (#3131, epic #3130). This file is the record of
WHICH concepts diverge and what was decided about each. `vocabulary-divergence.mjs`
reads it and fails when either surface grows a field with no entry here.
It is a JSON baseline rather than a doc under docs/ because the guard reads it:
one artefact, machine-checked, so the map cannot drift from what ships. The
`reason` on every entry is what keeps it readable by a person.
`value` on each side is `recorded` or `defaulted` (#3130 A3). Two entries can
share a column and still diverge, because one path substitutes a value the
other passes through -- that is the whole of the proofStatus and settled-at
defects, and a map keyed on columns alone could not say it.
`disposition` is about the NAMES. Two entries marked `converged` still record a
referent difference in their reason (`payment id` widens to sweep ids;
`token address` is normalised on one surface only). That second axis is
deliberately not counted -- the open number tracks the renames #3134 owes and the value defects #3132 does, not every
way two fields can disagree -- but a reader must not take `converged` as
'identical'.

receipt.label: MCP / SDK receipt
receipt.note: An SDK PRESENTATION layer, not a wire: the backend receipts wire is snake_case (#3130). A rename here reaches packages/mcp-server via listReceipts.

transaction.label: CLI / API transaction
transaction.note: The OpenAPI contract, already drift-gated by check:api-types. Read here rather than the generated core/src/api-types.ts so the guard fires where a developer adds the field.

cli.label: CLI --json output
cli.note: A THIRD surface, and a different axis from the two above: those pair a receipt FIELD with a transaction field; this one records the CASING CONVENTION each command emits. Kept as a separate section rather than forced into `concepts[]`, which has no place for it.

concepts.reason: One column, two values -- and the two names are ALIASES of the same `machine_payment_evidence.proof_status`, not two columns. It arrives through a LEFT JOIN, so with no evidence row the synthesized x402 path reports 'payment_confirmed' for a payment that has no receipt, while enrichment.ts passes the column through unchanged. Converging the NAMES before #3132 fixes the VALUE would hide the defect behind agreement. The substitution is conservative -- it never fabricates a settled state -- which is why this is a reconciliation defect and not a money-safety one.
Same concept, two names, both recorded. Unaffected by the #3132 fallback work, so #3134 may converge it independently.
Same concept, two names, both recorded. As above, not gated on #3132.

Unit AND fallback differ. Unlike the proof-state substitution this one FABRICATES a date: a payment that never confirmed reports its creation time as its settlement time, in a field the consumer reads as 'when this settled'. Same silent-substitution defect as proof state, opposite in severity.

DIFFERENT CONCEPTS that hold equal values on x402 rows by copy. Transaction.hash is the hash of ANY row in a wallet's history -- ERC-20 transfer, native transfer, internal call, delegate sweep, inbound deposit -- and only rows attributed to a payment intent carry a payment at all -- the attribution query has no rail filter, so `source` names which protocol it was ('x402', 'mpp_demo', 'mpp_crypto', 'spt') or 'direct' for a plain send. HavenPaymentReceipt.txHash is a payment field whose meaning is scheme-dependent and is already DEPRECATED for that reason (sdk/src/types.ts, #2998), with fundingTxHash/settlementTxHash as its successors. Renaming hash -> txHash would attach payment-settlement semantics to a generic transfer column and re-collapse the distinction #2998 paid to make.

DIFFERENT CONCEPTS. On non-payment rows `value` is the explorer's on-chain transfer value with `decimals` and `asset` beside it; `amountRaw` exists only on receipts. Equal on x402 rows by copy, different on the rest of the feed.
DIFFERENT CONCEPTS, same reasoning as atomic amount: valueFormatted is the formatted on-chain value of any transfer, amount is a payment figure.

One name on both surfaces, but not one referent: the receipt's payment_id is always a payment_intents.id, while the transaction's paymentId widens to a delegate_sweeps.id on activityType:'delegate_sweep' rows (enrichment.ts). Recorded as converged on the NAME; #3134 must not read it as 'same field' without that clause.
Already one name on both surfaces.

receipt.copiedFrom: payment_intents.token_address, copied onto machine_payment_evidence at settlement (modules/mpp/evidence.ts:321)

concepts.reason: Already one name on both surfaces. NOT both normalised, though: #3129 checksummed the TRANSACTION surface at its row boundary and touched no SDK file; the receipt surface passes the stored value through, checksummed by storage convention only -- the receipt reads machine_payment_evidence.token_address, a copy taken at settlement from payment_intents.token_address, which happens to be stored that way, while to_address and x402_merchant_address are stored lowercase.

receipt.derivedFrom: `payment_rail ?? source` at evidence-write time (modules/mpp/evidence.ts:173), stored on machine_payment_evidence.rail

transaction.by: infra/repositories/transaction-history.ts:225 substitutes 'direct'; modules/transactions/x402.ts:69 hardcodes 'x402' on the synthesized row, a second substitution site on the same field

concepts.reason: ONE axis. Both sides resolve the same two columns in the same order -- payment_rail then source -- so the receipt's `rail` is the payment PROTOCOL, exactly what the transaction calls `source`. An earlier draft filed them as permanently single-surface, reasoning that #1705 keeps three axes unmerged; that was wrong, because #1705's third axis is the ACCOUNT's execution_rail, which migration 036 states is a different axis from payment_intents.payment_rail. The asymmetry is one-sided and a later draft got it backwards: only the TRANSACTION side substitutes. It defaults to 'direct' in SQL and hardcodes 'x402' on the synthesized row. The receipt side cannot default, because when the coalesce yields a non-protocol rail recordMachinePaymentEvidenceBase returns not_applicable and no evidence row -- and therefore no receipt -- is written at all. (The `rail ?? 'unknown'` in evidence.ts is the FEE LEDGER's quoteFee call and never reaches a receipt.) #3132 owns the transaction-side substitutions before #3134 can rename anything.

$comment: Fields that exist on one surface and have no counterpart on the other, each
with the reason there will never be one. Without this list the guard's first
run would report 37 unpaired FIELDS (19 + 18, exactly) rather than the real
divergences, and a guard that cries wolf on its first run teaches people to
ignore it (#3131).

receipt.id: The evidence row's own identifier. A transaction row is not a database row.
receipt.fundingTxHash: Successor to the deprecated txHash (#2998), scheme-specific. No transfer-level counterpart.
receipt.settlementTxHash: Successor to the deprecated txHash (#2998), naming the merchant-side settlement leg specifically. No transfer-level counterpart.
receipt.chainId: Present on the ENRICHED transaction schema, not on transactionBaseProperties, which is the surface this guard reads.
receipt.payerAddress: #2960 party identity. The transaction row's `from` is the explorer's counterparty field, which is not the same question.
receipt.parties: #2960 structured party block. No transaction counterpart.
receipt.settlementAddress: Where settlement landed, scheme-specific. No transfer-level counterpart.
receipt.challengeId: x402 protocol state. Never appears on a wallet-history row.
receipt.idempotencyKey: Request-level key. Never appears on a wallet-history row.
receipt.selectedPayment: x402 protocol state -- which advertised requirement was chosen.
receipt.merchantStatus: The merchant's HTTP response state, not a chain fact.
receipt.createdAt: Evidence-row lifecycle. The transaction surface has one time field and #3132 owns its semantics.
receipt.paymentIntentId: Conditional key, present only when the raw row carries it. Links evidence to intent; no transfer-level counterpart.
receipt.approvalRequestId: Conditional key. Approval requests were dropped with the table (#2055); the field survives on the raw shape.

transaction.type: native / erc20 / internal -- a transfer classification. Receipts are always payments.
transaction.from: Explorer counterparty on explorer-derived rows; the account address on x402-synthesized rows. `payerAddress` is a party-identity field (#2960), not the same question.
transaction.to: Explorer counterparty on explorer-derived rows. On x402-synthesized rows there is no explorer: it holds x402_merchant_address ?? to_address, the same value the merchant-address concept pairs -- equal by copy, different concept, the framing this map already uses for `hash`.
transaction.asset: Ticker where known, falling back to the raw contract address on explorer rows; the intent's token_symbol verbatim on synthesized ones. Receipts carry tokenSymbol only.
transaction.decimals: Transfer formatting input. Receipts carry the formatted amount instead.
transaction.direction: in / out relative to the wallet. Every receipt is outbound by construction.
transaction.blockNumber: On-chain block of the transfer, or null (#3129). Receipts record no block.
transaction.isError: Whether the on-chain transfer reverted. A receipt exists only for a settled payment.
transaction.paymentFlowStatus: Derived by machinePaymentLifecycle from proof status and reconciliation events. Receipts expose the inputs, not the derivation.
transaction.activityType: delegate_sweep marker. Sweeps are not payments and have no receipt.
transaction.agentName: Attribution joined onto the history row. The receipt surface is agent-scoped already, so the agent is the principal rather than a field.
transaction.initiatedBy: #2097 initiator classification for any history row. Every receipt is agent-initiated by construction.
transaction.settlementScheme: eip3009 / erc7710 -- WHICH settlement branch moved the money (#1705). The three axes #1705 keeps unmerged are this, `source` (the payment protocol) and the ACCOUNT's `execution_rail` (account architecture) -- not the receipt's `rail`, which is the same axis as `source`.
transaction.amountSek: Book-time SEK value (#463) for the accounting feed.
transaction.fxRateSek: The rate amountSek was struck at (#2871).
transaction.accounting: Accounting-feed sync state joined by paymentId (#2870).

$comment: The CLI's `--json` casing split, declared rather than left as an accident
(#3133, owner decision 2026-09-18: KEEP the split — no rename, no dual-emit,
no breaking change). `/user/accounts` already took one breaking rename this
quarter (#2914/#3091), costing a dual-emit, a release boundary and a
dist-tags verification; a second to the same surface inside two epics is not
worth the tidiness. Normalising would also make the CLI stop being a
pass-through and start owning a presentation contract that diverges from the
OpenAPI response schema — which is what `interface Txn` already does badly.
ANCHORED ON FUNCTION NAMES, NOT LINE NUMBERS. #3133's own line anchors were
wrong three times across two correction passes; a guard keyed on them would
go red on an unrelated edit above, which trains people to update the anchor
rather than read it. The guard finds each envelope's enclosing function, so
the declaration survives any edit that does not move the emit itself.
PASS-THROUGH vs SELF-CONSTRUCTED. `emit()` forwards straight to the output
layer with no re-mapping, so a list command's casing IS the backend's and is
not the CLI's to choose. The `{ ok: true, … }` envelopes are the CLI's own
construction, and those are what this section ratchets.
Commands that forward the backend response unchanged. Their casing is the
OpenAPI response schema's, recorded here so the split is legible per command
-- recorded, not enforced: there is no CLI decision for a guard to hold.
ONE ENTRY IS NEITHER, and sits here only because it is not an envelope:
`activity export --format csv` builds its headers IN THE CLI over a camelCase
source (convention `snake-csv`), and it is the one entry in this section the
guard does check -- name for name and in order, against `const headers` in
commands.ts. It was declared here from the start with nothing comparing it to
the code, so the page could promise enforcement over a list free to drift.
`interface Safe` / `interface Txn` in commands.ts are a NON-EXHAUSTIVE subset
the CLI happens to read — the emitted JSON carries every key the backend
sends — so they are not the authoritative shape and must not be read as it.

wallets list.reason: Forwarded from GET /user/accounts unchanged (cmdWalletsList via accountsEnvelope). The casing is the backend's; the CLI does not re-map.

activity list.reason: Forwarded from GET /transactions unchanged (cmdActivityList). Same mechanism as wallets list, opposite convention, because the two backend surfaces differ — which is the divergence #3130 exists to record.

activity export --format csv.keys: date, type, status, direction, amount, token_symbol, token_address, counterparty_address, agent_name, tx_hash, chain_id, account_address
activity export --format csv.reason: A THIRD convention: snake_case CSV headers built in the CLI, over a camelCase JSON source. Headers are a file-format contract read by spreadsheets and importers, not a JSON shape, so they do not follow the payload they are derived from.

$comment: Object literals the CLI CONSTRUCTS ITSELF and passes to `emit()`, an `emit*`
helper, `d.o.data()` or `d.o.text()` -- its own shape, not the backend's.
One entry per emitting FUNCTION; a function emitting more than one
contributes all of their keys. The guard
censuses the source and fails when a function emits one that is not declared
here, so a new envelope cannot pick a convention by copying its neighbour.
The predicate is the LITERAL, not the `{ ok: true` prefix. Keying on that
prefix missed SEVEN EMITTERS -- functions, not call sites, which is the unit
this section is keyed on -- every one of which chooses a convention:
`cmdWalletsBalances`, `cmdWhoami`, the `emitGrant`/`emitRevoke` preparation
pair, `cmdAgentsConnect`, and the two export `meta` literals
(`cmdActivityExport`, `exportSie`) -- none of them carries an `ok` key. It
could not see a wrapped literal at all either. Seven, not three and not the
five a later draft wrote: this paragraph has now been wrong twice, the second
time while correcting the first, exactly as the deviceLogin entry below
records itself having done.
The guard compares KEY SETS, not only function names, so the `keys` string
on each entry is checked against the source. Comparing names alone let a key
be added to an ALREADY-declared envelope with a green run, leaving `reason`
describing a shape that no longer ships. Write `keys` as bare names, commas
between them and `;` between envelopes, with any aside in parentheses: a
group the parser cannot read is REFUSED, never silently shrunk.

cmdActivityExport.reason: The META half of `d.o.text(body, meta)`. output.ts wraps it as `{ ok: true, ...meta, content }`, so these ARE top-level --json keys even though the wrapper itself is built elsewhere -- which is why calling the whole export wrapper 'outside the census' hid them. Snake because `rows` is one word today and sets the precedent for the next key added here; the CSV headers inside `content` are a separate file-format contract with their own reason.

exportSie.reason: The SIE branch of the same export, and it passes NO `rows` -- the key set differs by format, which a reader who parsed one branch and assumed the other would get wrong. One key and no casing yet, declared so the next one has to choose rather than copy.

cmdGuide.reason: No multi-word key, so it exhibits no casing at all. Declared so the census covers every emitter rather than only the interesting ones, and so a key added here later has to choose deliberately.

deviceLogin.keys: ok, verification_url, user_code, device_code, interval, expires_at (the --no-wait device-start envelope); status, device_code, retry_after (the client-deadline pending envelope); ok, email, expires_at, user, apiBaseUrl (the completed-auth envelope)
deviceLogin.reason: Emits THREE envelopes, not two -- an earlier draft of this entry said two and undercounted its own subject while correcting someone else's count. Two are pure snake (device-start, and the pending envelope when the client deadline passes); the third mixes conventions inside a single object, expires_at beside apiBaseUrl. All three are declared because a function's second and third envelopes are just as much a convention choice as its first.

devicePollOnce.keys: status, device_code, retry_after (the still-pending envelope); ok, email, expires_at, user, apiBaseUrl (the completed-auth one)
devicePollOnce.reason: Also two: a snake pending envelope and the shared completed-auth literal that mixes expires_at with apiBaseUrl.

cmdLogin.reason: The completed-auth literal again -- the third of the three sites that mix expires_at with apiBaseUrl inside one object.

cmdLogout.reason: Pure snake. #3133 listed this among the auth envelopes that mix; it does not — it carries no camel key. Recorded because the correction matters: the intra-object mixing is THREE sites, not four.

cmdAgentLifecycle.reason: Pause/resume. #3133 called this function cmdAgentPauseResume; the name is cmdAgentLifecycle. Its anchor correction was right that this is not the revoke site.

cmdAgentRevoke.reason: Hybrid envelope: a bare `ok` beside snake_case identifiers.

cmdAgentRename.reason: Hybrid envelope: a bare `ok` beside a snake_case identifier, same shape as cmdAgentRevoke on the rename verb.

cmdWalletRename.reason: Hybrid envelope on the wallet noun — `account_id`, the post-#2914 spelling, beside a bare `ok`.

cmdContactsRemove.reason: Hybrid envelope on the contact noun: `contact_id` beside a bare `ok` and a bare `removed`.

cmdWhoami.reason: Pure snake, and notably `api_url` here against `apiBaseUrl` in the auth envelopes -- the same concept under two spellings on the same surface. Declared rather than converged: #3133's decision is that the split stays. The literal is pure snake; it also spreads the backend profile object, so the emitted JSON carries whatever keys that carries.

cmdWalletsBalances.reason: The one command that RE-MAPS: it reads safe.chain_id from the backend and emits chainId. So the CLI is a pass-through everywhere except here, which is why the documentation states that exception rather than claiming a blanket rule.

emitGrant.reason: Budget-grant preparation. Self-constructed snake keys with no `ok`, so an `{ ok: true` census could not see it. The literal is snake; it spreads the backend build object, so the emitted JSON carries that too.

emitRevoke.keys: agent_id, delegation_hash, status (spread over the prepared backend response)
emitRevoke.reason: Revocation preparation: CLI-chosen snake keys spread over a whole backend response. Neither a plain envelope nor a plain pass-through, and invisible to an `{ ok: true` census.

cmdAgentsConnect.keys: setup_id, approval_url, connector_command, connector_exit_code, outcome, relay
cmdAgentsConnect.reason: The whole user-visible result of `agents connect --run --json`. Built into a local `const` and handed to an emit helper rather than written inline, which is why an inline-only census could not see it -- `connector_exit_code` and `relay` are invented here and come back from no backend under those names. `outcome` is a NESTED object (ConnectorOutcome) and only the container key is recorded -- its own keys are read by scripts too, and are outside this census the way every nested literal is.

$comment: Shapes the census cannot reach, each with the reason it cannot. Not `--json`
command output in the `commands.ts` sense: two are built in `output.ts`, which
the scanner does not read, and one is a file on disk that no release channel
can rewrite.
`keys` here is PROSE and is not parsed -- these entries are documentation,
not inputs to the key-set comparison the `envelopes` entries go through.

credential file account address.keys: account_address, with a permanent safe_address fallback
credential file account address.reason: packages/connect/src/doctor.ts declares both keys and reads the pre-#2908 name permanently (#2906 decision 2a): the next --rekey or setup rewrites it as account_address, but an un-rekeyed install keeps the old spelling forever. No release channel can reach it.

export wrapper.keys: ok, format, content — plus rows on the CSV branch only
export wrapper.reason: Built in packages/cli/src/output.ts, not commands.ts, so it is outside the census by construction -- the scanner reads one file. It wraps BOTH the CSV and the SIE export -- and the SIE branch passes no `rows`, so the key set differs by format -- and a reader who only saw the header list would parse the wrong thing: the body is inside `content`.

failure envelope.reason: Also built in output.ts, and the single most-parsed --json shape an agent sees, because it is what every failed command returns. Outside the census for the same structural reason as the export wrapper, and recorded here so 'what does a failure look like' has an answer on this page.
